channel.title: Said & Checked: South Dakota — AskAmerica
channel.description: What officeholders said each day from or about South Dakota, and which statements government data supports, contradicts or rules out.

item.title: Said & Checked, South Dakota, 2026-11-18: none false or contradicted, 2 unsettled (John Thune)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • John Thune, U.S. Senator from South Dakota: “The local water company identified vulnerabilities in this 60-year-old sewer pipe a full 7 years before it burst, but proposed repairs languished in the Federal permitting process year after year after year.” Unsettled. DC Water says it asked the National Park Service in 2018 for a categorical exclusion to rehabilitate the pipe, NPS required an Environmental Assessment in 2021, and the assessment was not finished when the pipe collapsed (as reported by WJLA from the Washington Post). NPS says it received DC Water's proposal only in December 2025, and DC Water says its inspections showed no imminent failure, so the cause of the delay is disputed.
  • John Thune, U.S. Senator from South Dakota: “And if a NEPA lawsuit is filed over a proposed project, it takes almost 2 years to resolve it.” Unsettled. Studies differ by method. The Breakthrough Institute reports an average of 4.2 years from permit to the end of appellate challenges, and other studies give medians of roughly 1.5 to 2 years for court cases. 'Almost 2 years' fits a median reading, not the appellate average.

12 statements by 3 officeholders. 11 checked: 9 supported, 2 unsettled · 1 not checkable.

item.title: Said & Checked, South Dakota, 2026-11-17: none false or contradicted, 1 unsupported, 6 unsettled (John Thune)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsupported and Unsettled

  • John Thune, U.S. Senator from South Dakota (Senate Majority Leader): “we have confirmed 606 civilian nominees.” Unsupported. No count of civilian nominees confirmed in this Congress as of Nov. 16 was found; the nearest published figures are 301 confirmed en bloc as of May 2026 and 417 confirmations in 2025. The search covered web sources, a May 2026 Senate Republican leadership release and Senate vote pages; the majority leader's nominations tracker was not read.
  • John Thune, U.S. Senator from South Dakota (Senate Majority Leader): “we have already locked in floor votes for every available judicial nominee.” Unsettled. Senate roll calls 261 and 262 confirm cloture votes on two circuit nominees on Nov. 12, but the Senate executive calendar could not be read, so whether every judicial nominee on it had a vote scheduled was not confirmed.
  • John Thune, U.S. Senator from South Dakota (Senate Majority Leader): “That includes getting the President's Cabinet in place at the fastest pace in over 20 years, in half the time--half the time--it took to fill the Obama and first Trump administration Cabinets.” Unsettled. Ballotpedia reports all 15 Cabinet secretaries confirmed by March 10, 2025, about 49 days in, the fastest of presidents since 2009; reported figures of about 97 days for Trump's first term and 98 for Obama's fit 'half the time.' No comparison reaching back to 2005 was found, so 'fastest in over 20 years' is not settled.

12 statements by 1 officeholder. 11 checked: 4 supported, 6 unsettled, 1 unsupported · 1 not checkable.
